measured.name: D
measured.note: how many dimensions square-4 has

measured.name: DEG
measured.note: the ways out of a point on square-4 - the exits it has, counted

measured.name: SHEET
measured.note: the exits with no component along the pulsing axis, which is what a source emits over. NOT DEG, which is 4

measured.name: CYCLE
measured.note: how many steps go round the ring of a turn on square-4

measured.name: slice
measured.note: a turn sweeps a PLANE, and a plane needs two dimensions - so what a turn lives in is min(D, 2), which is 2 here and stops growing at 2 however many dimensions are added

measured.name: \bar{c}
measured.note: a step's worth of lean is what one annihilation buys a path, and a step is \bar{c} - one cell a tick, the lattice's own speed. Its value in those units is one, which is a statement about the units and not about the quantity

steps.because: an annihilation gives the direction it went one extra way of being taken, so after n of them that direction has 1 + n ways against the 1 each that the DEG alternatives still have. The surplus is n, each worth a step, against DEG - and a path's lean is that. Note what is NOT here: nothing divides by anything that grows with n, so the lean is linear in the count and has no ceiling

lean(n).says: how much a path through the place leans, after n of them

n.says: how many annihilations have happened there

\\bar{c}.says: a step - one cell a tick

DEG.says: the ways out of a point - the alternatives not taken
